description: Saturation analysis for rest-wrapper. Run find-saturation.sh for automated sweep. Panels turn orange/red when thresholds are crossed. Saturation = RPS flatlines while latency climbs.

panels.description: Requests per second served by rest-wrapper (server-side). Saturation signal: stops growing despite more VUs.
panels.title: Current RPS

panels.description: Mean HTTP response time measured by k6. Saturation signal: rises steeply (>200ms orange, >500ms red).
panels.title: Mean Response Time

panels.description: Combined user+system CPU for rest-wrapper process. Saturation signal: >80% (red). Node.js is single-threaded so user CPU is the primary constraint.
panels.title: App CPU (user+sys)

panels.description: Fraction of time the Node.js event loop is busy (0=idle, 1=fully saturated). Saturation signal: >80% (red) means the event loop has no headroom.
panels.title: Event Loop Utilization

panels.description: Fraction of k6 upsert checks that passed (1.0 = all pass). Saturation signal: drops below 99% (red) meaning the service is returning errors under load.

targets.expr: sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Upsert should return status is 201",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Upsert should return status is 201",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

panels.title: K6 Upsert Check Pass Rate

panels.description: P90 event loop delay: how long callbacks wait before executing. Saturation signal: >10ms (orange) = pressure; >50ms (red) = severe backlog.
panels.title: Event Loop Delay P90

panels.description: Server-side RPS (left axis) overlaid with active VU count (right axis). Saturation: RPS flatlines or drops while VUs keep increasing.
panels.title: RPS vs VUs — Saturation: RPS flatlines as VUs rise

panels.description: Mean response time from k6. Threshold lines: 200ms (orange) and 500ms (red). Saturation: response time starts climbing steeply — the knee-of-curve is the saturation point.
panels.title: Response Time Trend — Knee = saturation point

panels.description: CPU utilization (user + system stacked) and event loop utilization as separate lines. Red threshold at 80%. If event loop hits limit before CPU, Node.js I/O is the bottleneck; if CPU hits first, computation is the bottleneck.
panels.title: CPU (stacked) & Event Loop Utilization — hit 80% = saturated

panels.description: Event loop callback delay: how long tasks wait in the queue before executing. Mean, P90, and Max. Red threshold at 50ms. Rising delay means the event loop queue is growing — a classic Node.js saturation symptom.
panels.title: Event Loop Delay — >10ms pressure, >50ms saturated

panels.description: Average time k6 requests spend waiting for a TCP connection slot. Should be ~0ms at healthy load. Rising blocked time means the OS connection queue or network is the bottleneck, not the app.
panels.title: K6 Blocked Time — >1ms = connection pressure, >10ms = network bottleneck

panels.description: Pass rate for each k6 check. All should stay at 100%. Any drop below 99% (red threshold line) means the service is returning incorrect or failed responses under load — a hard saturation boundary.

targets.expr: sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Upsert should return status is 201",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Upsert should return status is 201",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return status is 200 or 206",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return status is 200 or 206",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return elapsed time data points",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return elapsed time data points",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct time range in data points",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct time range in data points",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct tag in data points",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct tag in data points",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct nV value in data points",condition="nonzero"}) / sum without(condition)(k6_checks_total{service_name="k6",check="Query should return correct nV value in data points",condition=~"nonzero|zero"})

panels.title: K6 Check Pass Rates — any drop below 99% line = correctness failure at this load

panels.description: Iteration throughput (left) vs VUs (right). Healthy scaling: iterations/sec grow proportionally with VUs. Saturation: iterations/sec flattens while VUs keep increasing — queuing theory in action.
panels.title: Iteration Throughput vs VUs — flatline = queuing

title: rest-wrapper Saturation Analysis
